title: Waterfalls Actually Destroy Themselves From the Inside Out
description: Discover the incredible geological process of how waterfalls march backward, carving deep gorges over thousands of years.
instagram_caption: Waterfalls look permanent, but they're actually marching backward! 🌊🪨 Discover the hidden geological war that shapes our planet's most dramatic landscapes. #geology #naturelovers #earthscience #waterfalls

segments.narration: Waterfalls look permanent, but they are actually marching backward, slowly retreating upstream and destroying themselves as they go.
broll_queries: rushing water flowing over cliff edge

segments.narration: This happens because tough rock sits on top of soft stone, which easily erodes as water plunges over the edge.
broll_queries: cross section rock layers waterfall cliff
close up water hitting rock layers
geological rock strata waterfall side view

segments.narration: Below, in the violent plunge pool, trapped rocks swirl like natural drill bits, grinding away the soft lower stone.
broll_queries: extreme close up swirling water bubbles
underwater swirling rocks and sand current
violent water churning bottom of waterfall

segments.narration: Without support underneath, the heavy upper rock eventually yields to gravity in one sudden, catastrophic collapse.
broll_queries: crumbling cliff rocks falling into water

segments.narration: Over thousands of years, this continuous cycle of collapse and retreat carves massive gorges deep into the landscape.

wide shot sheer cliffs canyon river

segments.narration: It is a powerful reminder of nature's relentless patience. Subscribe to Wonders of the Nature for more.
